title: Cartesian clopen lifts and equivalence of varying-ring inverse image
statement: Let $R_n$ be arbitrary commutative rings with maps $\varphi_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$, and use the ordinary semilinear module-system categories $\mathscr S_X$ and the specified inverse-image composition and identity comparisons of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. For every isomorphism of schemes $s:U\to X$, the functor $s^*:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_U$ is an equivalence with quasi-inverse $(s^{-1})^*$. Its two inverse comparisons are induced by the specified inverse-image compositors, equality transport along $s^{-1}s=1$ and $ss^{-1}=1$, and the specified ordinary identity comparisons. If $pk=ir$ is a cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $p:W\to T$, $r:V\to S$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then its canonical lift $s=(k,r):V\to W\times_TS$ is an isomorphism. Thus its ordinary inverse image, with those same comparisons, is an equivalence. No hypothesis on coefficient flatness or finiteness is required.

proof.text: Put $t=s^{-1}:X\to U$, $F=s^*:\mathscr S_X\to\mathscr S_U$ and $H=t^*:\mathscr S_U\to\mathscr S_X$. For composable $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to C$, denote the specified ordinary inverse-image compositor by $c_{a,b}:(b\circ a)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*\circ b^*$ and the specified identity comparison by $e_A:(\mathrm{id}_A)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S_A}$. Define the two natural isomorphisms by the actual composites $$u_X:HF\xrightarrow{c_{t,s}^{-1}}(s\circ t)^*\xrightarrow{s\circ t=\mathrm{id}_X}(\mathrm{id}_X)^*\xrightarrow{e_X}\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S_X},\qquad u_U:FH\xrightarrow{c_{s,t}^{-1}}(t\circ s)^*\xrightarrow{t\circ s=\mathrm{id}_U}(\mathrm{id}_U)^*\xrightarrow{e_U}\mathrm{id}_{\mathscr S_U}.$$ The middle arrows are equality transports. Each arrow is an isomorphism of functors on the ordinary system categories, so these composites are natural isomorphisms there; in particular their components are morphisms of semilinear systems, not merely families of levelwise morphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-quasi-inverse-hom-bijection] to $F,H,u_X,u_U$: for all objects $M,M\prime$ of $\mathscr S_X$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(M,M\prime)\to\operatorname{Hom}(FM,FM\prime)$ is bijective. Every $N\in\mathscr S_U$ is isomorphic to $F(HN)$, using the inverse of $(u_U)_N$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] hold, in a common sufficiently large universe, and $F$ is an equivalence. The already specified functor $H=t^*$ is a quasi-inverse witnessed by $u_X$ and $u_U$, so the inverse comparisons are precisely the composites in step 1. No triangle identity for arbitrary chosen inverse comparisons is assumed.

Write $P=W\times_T S$ with projections $b:P\to W$ and $q:P\to S$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $s=(k,r):V\to P$ has $b\circ s=k$ and $q\circ s=r$. Since the given square is cartesian, its vertex $V$ with maps $k,r$ also has this same universal property. It therefore gives a unique $v:P\to V$ with $k\circ v=b$ and $r\circ v=q$. The maps $s\circ v$ and $\mathrm{id}_P$ have the same composites with $b,q$, hence are equal by uniqueness for $P$. Likewise $v\circ s$ and $\mathrm{id}_V$ have the same composites with $k,r$, hence are equal by uniqueness for $V$. Consequently $s$ is an isomorphism with inverse $v$. This calculation only uses the cartesian hypothesis; the stated properness and quasi-compact open hypotheses need no additional consequence here.

proof.text: Apply steps 1 and 2 to the scheme isomorphism $s:V\to P$ from step 3 and its inverse $v$. This gives $s^*:\mathscr S_P\to\mathscr S_V$ with quasi-inverse $v^*$ and exactly the same ordinary compositor--equality-transport--identity comparisons. The constructions and the cited equivalence criteria do not tensor along $R_{n+1}\to R_n$, take derived functors, or restrict the systems. Thus arbitrary rings and arbitrary transition ring maps allowed by [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] suffice, with no coefficient flatness or finiteness assumption.
